body.p: There was a hero named Nurgowul, a rifleman. He defeated a camp, he killed the boys, he took the girls for himself. In the morning he wandered off, he arrived at a yurt. He saw an old woman holding her child, he asked her: "Is your child a boy or a girl?" "A girl!" Nurgowul went off saying: "If it is a boy, he shall follow my marks!" After Nurgowul had gone, the [boy's] father came. The father began to teach his son to dodge. He took off the coat of his son, he pelted him with fire and coal, that one dodged. Then the father made an arrow, he shot with it, his son dodged. After the son had made arrows for himself, when he was seventeen years old, he went along Nurgowul's marks. He was going for thirty days. On the thirtieth [day] he heard bells ringing. He saw and recognized his elder sister. His elder sister were dragging an animal, which Nurgowul had killed. His sisters told where Nurgowol is living. He ate some meat, he went to Nurgowul. When coming closer he stalked and whistled. Nurgowul took his arrow, he compared it and said: "Spread a mat, shoot, man who has come from far away". "You start, old man." Nurgowul shot and missed. The other one shot through his knee. Nurgowul shot again and missed. The other one tore our Nurgowul's intestines. Nurgowul said: "You have come, when I have turned old", he give [him] his arrows and said: "Defeat the camps, like I [did]". [DCh]: Imperative morphology is missing in the last clause. The boy caught his [= Nurgowul's] reindeer, he brought his sisters home.
